Solving a small MDP by hand

Once the policy is fixed, the Bellman equations are ordinary linear equations: one per state, with the values as unknowns. With two states that is two equations in two unknowns, which you can solve with school algebra, or see as two lines crossing.

Lesson 17's two-state weather ($p$ and $q$ are its $a$ and $b$), now with rewards: every sunny day pays $r_\text{S}$, every rainy day pays $r_\text{R}$. No actions to choose (the policy is fixed), so each state has one row of transition probabilities. The task never ends, and $\gamma < 1$ keeps the return finite.

Each equation is a line in the plane of possible values $(v_\text{S}, v_\text{R})$. Only the crossing point satisfies both. Click anywhere to place a guess, then press "Back up" to replace the guess by the right-hand sides.

The maths

With the policy fixed, Lesson 26's equation becomes $v(s) = r(s) + \gamma \sum_{s'} P_{ss'}\, v(s')$, where $r(s)$ is the expected reward from $s$ and $P_{ss'}$ is the probability of moving from $s$ to $s'$. For the two weather states:

$$\begin{aligned} v_\text{S} &= r_\text{S} + \gamma\big[(1 - p)\, v_\text{S} + p\, v_\text{R}\big] \\ v_\text{R} &= r_\text{R} + \gamma\big[q\, v_\text{S} + (1 - q)\, v_\text{R}\big] \end{aligned}$$

Move the unknowns to the left:

$$\begin{aligned} \big(1 - \gamma(1 - p)\big)\, v_\text{S} - \gamma p\, v_\text{R} &= r_\text{S} \\ -\gamma q\, v_\text{S} + \big(1 - \gamma(1 - q)\big)\, v_\text{R} &= r_\text{R} \end{aligned}$$

Two linear equations, so two straight lines. Solving them (Cramer's rule) gives

$$\begin{aligned} D &= \big(1 - \gamma(1-p)\big)\big(1 - \gamma(1-q)\big) - \gamma^2 p q \\ v_\text{S} &= \frac{\big(1 - \gamma(1-q)\big)\, r_\text{S} + \gamma p\, r_\text{R}}{D} \\ v_\text{R} &= \frac{\big(1 - \gamma(1-p)\big)\, r_\text{R} + \gamma q\, r_\text{S}}{D} \end{aligned}$$

Expanding $D$ gives $D = (1-\gamma)\big(1 - \gamma + \gamma(p + q)\big)$, which is positive whenever $\gamma < 1$. So the lines always cross at exactly one point. At $\gamma = 1$ the return of a never-ending task can be infinite and $D = 0$.

"Back up" applies $v \leftarrow r + \gamma P v$ to your guess. The error after a press is $\gamma P$ times the error before. Each row of $P$ averages, so the larger of the two errors shrinks by at least a factor $\gamma$ per press, and the purple path closes in on the crossing. Lesson 30 turns that into an algorithm.
